label: IX.8, 1049b4–1050b6 — Actuality is prior in account and substance, and qualifiedly in time
interpretation: Aristotle distinguishes three senses at the outset. The account of capacity refers to its exercise. The substance comparison uses mature form and actuality as end. The temporal case uses generation or acquisition from an already actual source, with the prior actual and what comes to be the same in kind rather than number.
attribution: The passage states that actuality is prior to the corresponding capacity in account and in substance and that in time, an already actual member of the same kind can precede the capacity, although a subject’s own capacity can precede its own actuality, which is the premise.
